headline: Approved pay rates for election workers and Presiding Officers, and the election worker list for 11 August 2026.
summary: The meeting reviewed the 11 August 2026 election schedule, absentee ballot counts, and rules for poll watchers, ICE, press, political signs, politics, and firearms at polling places. Members approved the minutes of 21 February 2026, the list of election workers, and pay rates for election workers and Presiding Officers.
decisions: Approved the minutes of 21 February 2026, with all present members voting in favor.
Approved the list of election workers for 11 August 2026, with all present members voting in favor.
Approved pay at the State minimum hourly wage for election workers and the State minimum hourly wage plus $5.00 for Presiding Officers, with all present members voting in favor.

decision_titles: List of election workers for 11 August 2026
Pay rates for election workers and Presiding Officers
plain_text:
PAGE 1 
BOARD OF CIVIL AUTHORITY 
DRAFT MINUTES 
3 AUGUST 2026 
 
The South Burlington Board of Civil Authority held a meeting on 3 August 2026, 
at 5:00 p.m., in Room 301, City Hall, 180 Market St. 
Members Present: C. Shaw, Chair; T. Barritt, D. Kinville, L. Bailey, A. Chalnick, H. 
Rees, A. Pugh, M. Vigneau, E. Fitzgerald, M. St. Germain   
Also Present: S. Hinckley 
1. Welcome: 
Mr. Shaw welcomed members to the meeting. 
2. Review evacuation plans in case of an emergency. 
Ms. Reese reviewed emergency plans. 
3. Approve Minutes from 21 February 2026: 
Mr. Chalnick moved to approve the Minutes of 21 February 2026 as presented.  
Mr. St. Germain seconded.  The motion passed with all present voting in favor. 
4. Review Election Master Schedule for 11 August 2026: 
Ms. Rees noted there has been a lot of confusion about this election.  Some voters 
are asking for only the State Primary ballot or only the local ballot.  Because of 
this, there will be 2 separate checklists, one for the State ballot and one for the 
local ballot.  Ms. Rees also suggested there not be pre-processing of ballots that 
have been received.  She then reviewed the process as to how voters will be given 
ballots and how they will proceed to vote. 
Ms. Hinckley noted that there have been a number of ballots received that have 
not been returned correctly (e.g., all the ballots in one envelope).  Ms. Rees said 
these voters have been notified and invited to come in and correct their errors.  
Some have not been willing to do this.  Their envelopes will be sent to the polls in 
case they do show up there.
BOARD OF CIVIL AUTHORITY 3 AUGUST 2026 PAGE 2 
Ms. Rees noted that people who are declaring themselves as “write-in 
candidates” have until Thursday to turn in their petitions.  There will be 
information in the binders on Election Day as to how to specifically handle votes 
for those candidates. 
5. Approve list of election workers for 11 August 2026: 
Mr. Chalnick moved to approve the list of election workers for 11 August 2026 as 
presented.  Mr. Barritt seconded.  Motion passed with all present voting in favor. 
6. Confirm Rate of Pay for Presiding Officers and Election Workers: 
Mr. Barritt suggested the State minimum wage for election workers and the State 
minimum wage plus $5.00 for Presiding Officers. 
Mr. St. Germain then moved to pay election workers the State minimum hourly 
wage and Presiding Officers the State minimum hourly wage plus $5.00.  Mr. 
Chalnick seconded.  The motion passed with all present voting in favor. 
7. Review of Policies: 
a. Poll Watchers: 
Ms. Rees said she did not anticipate there being poll watchers at the Primary 
Election and noted that the City’s policy should be updated before the November 
election. 
Ms. Kinville said the main point is that poll watchers cannot interfere with the 
check-in table.  Ms. Rees said there will be a spot identified for them.  Mr. Shaw 
added that poll watchers should identify which candidate or which issue they are 
there for. 
b. ICE at the Polls: 
Ms. Rees said she has had a number of calls regarding protection of ballots.  She 
stressed that ICE is not allowed in the building, and they cannot impede voters 
going into or out of the building.  There will be phone numbers available for the 
Secretary of State’s Office, the State Police, and the local Police if a concern 
arises. 
c. Press at the Polls: 
Members of the Press must stay far enough away so they do not photograph 
people’s ballots.  They should remain behind the barrier. 
d. Political Signs:
BOARD OF CIVIL AUTHORITY 3 AUGUST 2026 PAGE 3 
Public Works is responsible for signage.  Signs can be put out 2 days before the 
election and must be removed after the election.  A candidate who has been 
putting signs on trees and telephone poles has been instructed to remove them. 
e. Politics at the Polling Place: 
People entering to vote can have “slogans” on caps or shirts as long as the 
candidate’s name is not included.  There will be identified areas for candidates to 
stand at the polling places. 
f. Firearms: 
No firearms may be brought into a polling place.  If an issue arises, call the Police. 
8. Confirm current absentee ballot issuance and return rates: 
As of today, 1,234 State Primary ballots have been issued, and 662 have been 
returned.  1,135 local ballots have been issued, and 694 have been returned. 
9. Discussion of Early Processing Needs: 
Members agreed not to have a pre-processing session. 
10. Other Business: 
Ms. Rees noted that the Food Shelf will be doing a drive at each polling location. 
Ms. Rees also noted that 2 candidates are Board members.  They have been asked 
that they not be there when the polls are open and not have their names posted 
anywhere. 
Ms. Bailey and Mr. Shaw volunteered to deliver ballots to anyone who calls in 
with a disability that will keep them going to the polls. 
As there was no further business to come before the Board, Mr. Chalnick                      
moved to adjourn.  Ms. Pugh seconded.  The meeting was adjourned at             
5:48 p.m. 
 
 
                                               __________________________, Clerk
